topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines the learning objectives regarding cancer therapy modalities.

topics.label: Conventional local and cytotoxic cancer therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the mechanisms, clinical successes, toxicities, and resistance mechanisms of traditional cancer treatments, including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy.

topics.label: Exploiting cellular vulnerabilities and repair defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine therapeutic strategies that exploit intrinsic biological vulnerabilities in cancer cells, including hormone dependence, cell cycle checkpoint deficiencies, and DNA repair defects.

topics.label: Targeting oncogenic kinase drivers and mechanisms of resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on identifying oncogenic driver mutations and using small-molecule kinase inhibitors to target them, alongside the resistance pathways that emerge during treatment.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibody and antibody-drug conjugate therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the use of engineered monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates to specifically bind cancer cell surface antigens and deliver cytotoxic effects.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and T-cell-directed interventions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the principles of natural immune surveillance and detail immunotherapeutic strategies that harness and engineer T cells to eradicate tumors.

topics.label: Challenges, historical progress, and future directions in cancer management
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the broader complexities of cancer treatment, reflecting on historical survival gains, prevention strategies, and emerging paradigms for future therapy.
